title: Vain Are the Hopes That Rebels Place
description: Vain Are the Hopes That Rebels Place in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 99, headed “Stones made children of Abraham; or, Grace not conveyed by religious parents, Matt. 3. 9”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Vain are the hopes that re-bels place Up-on their birth and blood, De-scend-ed from a pi-ous race; (Their fa-thers now with God.)

lines: Vain are the hopes that rebels place
He from the caves of earth and hell
And fill the house of Abra'm well
Such wondrous power doth he possess
Who call'd the world from emptiness,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
